problem:
Evaluate the double integral ${∬}_{D}9{x}^{2}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A,$ where 
$D={(x,y)\,:\,-2\le x\le 2,\,-1\le y\le 1}.$

examples.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Double Integral Over a Rectangular Domain
examples.problem:
Evaluate the double integral $\displaystyle \iint \limits_{D} \dfrac y{x^2} \, \textrm d A$, where 
$D=\left\{ (x,y) \: : \:2 \leq x \leq 4,\: 0 \leq y \leq 3\right\}.$
examples.worked_solution:
First, we express our double integral as a repeated integral:    

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\frac{y}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{3}[{\int }_{2}^{4}\frac{y}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3}[{\int }_{2}^{4}\frac{y}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{[-\frac{y}{x}]}_{2}^{4}\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}(-\frac{y}{4}-(-\frac{y}{2}))\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{y}{4}\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{y}{4}\,\text{d}y & ={[\frac{{y}^{2}}{8}]}_{0}^{3} \\  & =\frac{{3}^{2}}{8}-\frac{{0}^{2}}{8} \\  & =\frac{9}{8}\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{y}{1+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{2}y[{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}y[\operatorname{arctan}⁡x]_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}y(\operatorname{arctan}⁡1-\operatorname{arctan}⁡0)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{\pi }{4}y\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

 

Then, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{\pi }{4}y\,\text{d}y & =\frac{\pi }{4}{[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{8}({2}^{2}-{0}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}\end{aligned}
$$
